schemes.name: ADIP Scheme (Assistance to Disabled Persons for Purchase/Fitting of Aids and Appliances)
schemes.summary: Central Sector scheme that subsidises assistive devices such as hearing aids, smart canes, wheelchairs, prostheses and smartphones for persons with disabilities.

notes: Applicant must hold a UDID card or UDID enrolment number with at least 40% disability.
Aadhaar or Aadhaar enrolment number is required.
Above ₹30,000 monthly family income the scheme does not provide a subsidy.

benefits: Up to ₹15,000 for aids and assistive devices, once in 3 years.
Up to ₹50,000 subsidy for motorised tricycles or motorised wheelchairs, once in 5 years.
documents_required: UDID card or UDID enrolment number
Income proof for the subsidy slab
how_to_apply: Register or log in on the ARJUN portal (adip.depwd.gov.in).
Select the required aid or appliance and the nearest implementing agency.
Attend the assessment at the implementing agency or PMD-VK centre.
Collect the device after approval; do not pay the subsidised portion twice.
notes: Income slabs and benefit caps were read from the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities page on 2026-11-18.
The page states the scheme was last revised on 26.09.2024.
Re-check after 31 March 2027 or whenever the department publishes a new revision.

schemes.name: UDID Card (Unique Disability ID / Swavlamban Card)
schemes.summary: A single digital disability identity card issued through the Swavlamban portal, intended to replace multiple state-level disability certificates.

notes: Any person with a recognised disability can apply.
The medical assessment decides the certified disability percentage.
Aadhaar is used for identity verification.

benefits: Single card accepted for disability-related benefits across states.
Used to apply for ADIP devices, scholarships and pension schemes.
Supports rail and state transport concession claims, subject to the operator's current rules.
documents_required: Medical reports or existing disability certificate
how_to_apply: Fill the disability application and choose a nearby medical authority.
Download the e-UDID card after approval.
schemes.helpline: Check the Swavlamban portal contact page
notes: Do not state that the card is free; fees and timelines vary by state and assessment centre.
Do not promise a specific rail concession percentage; categories differ.

schemes.name: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
schemes.summary: Rights-based law covering 21 recognised disabilities, non-discrimination, accessibility and reservation in employment and higher education.

notes: Applies to persons with one or more of the 21 recognised disabilities.
Reservation in government establishments is 4% for persons with benchmark disabilities.
Reservation in higher education institutions is 5%.

benefits: 4% reservation in government establishments for benchmark disabilities.
5% reservation in government and government-aided higher education institutions.
Protection from discrimination and a right to accessible public infrastructure.
Accessibility obligations for public transport, buildings and government websites.
documents_required: Disability certificate or UDID card for reservation claims
Proof of disability category for the specific reservation
how_to_apply: For employment reservation, follow the recruiting body's notification and attach the disability certificate.
For education reservation, apply through the institution's admission process and attach the certificate.
For discrimination complaints, approach the relevant State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities.
schemes.helpline: State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities
notes: The Act text is stable; reservation implementation notifications change, so cite the recruiting body's notice.
Do not describe the 4% and 5% figures as applying to all posts or all institutions without checking the notification.

schemes.name: Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan (Accessible India Campaign)
schemes.summary: A national campaign to improve accessibility of the built environment, transport and information and communication systems.

notes: This is an infrastructure and standards campaign, not a cash benefit.
It does not provide individual devices or pensions.

benefits: Accessibility standards for buildings, transport and government websites.
Tactile paving, ramps, lifts and accessible toilets in public infrastructure.
Auditory and visual announcements in supported transport systems.
how_to_apply: There is no individual application. Report an inaccessible public facility to the local municipal body or the department's grievance channel.
notes: Do not present this as a device grant or a cash transfer.
Do not claim a specific number of retrofitted stations without a dated source.
